cues.en: We're going to break a rule. We're breaking one of the rules of Numberphile.
cues.zh: 我们要破个例。我们要打破 Numberphile 的一条规矩。

cues.en: We're talking about something that isn't a number. We're going to talk about infinity.
cues.zh: 我们要聊的东西不是数字。我们要聊的是无穷。

cues.en: So infinity.
cues.zh: 那么，无穷。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: like I said, infinity
cues.zh: 就像我说的，无穷

cues.en: is not a number.
cues.zh: 不是数字。

cues.en: Right? It's a idea. It's a concept. It's the idea of being
cues.zh: 对吧？它是一个想法。一个概念。它指的是

cues.en: endless, of going on forever. I think everyone's familiar with the idea of infinity, even kids. You start counting one, two, three, four, five. You know, you might be five years old, but already you're thinking, what's the biggest number I can think of? And you go, oh, it's 20.
cues.zh: 无尽、永远延续下去。我觉得每个人都熟悉无穷这个概念，连小孩也是。你开始数一、二、三、四、五。你可能才五岁，但已经在想：我能想到的最大的数字是什么？然后你说，哦，是 20。

cues.en: You get a bit old and you go, maybe it's a million. It never ends, does it? Because you can keep adding one. So that's the idea of infinity.
cues.zh: 你长大一点，又会说，也许是一百万。它永远不会结束，对吧？因为你可以一直加一。这就是无穷的概念。

cues.en: The numbers go on forever.
cues.zh: 数字可以永远延续下去。

cues.en: But I'm going tell you one of the more surprising
cues.zh: 但我要告诉你一个更令人惊讶的

cues.en: facts about infinity.
cues.zh: 关于无穷的事实。

cues.en: There are different kinds of infinity. Some infinities
cues.zh: 无穷有不同的种类。有些无穷

cues.en: are bigger than others.
cues.zh: 比另一些更大。

cues.en: Let's have a look. The first type of infinity
cues.zh: 我们来看看。第一种无穷

cues.en: is called countable,
cues.zh: 叫可数无穷，

cues.en: and I don't like the name countable.
cues.zh: 但我不喜欢“可数”这个名字。

cues.en: And Brady gave me a little bit of a just then, because if you're talking about infinity,
cues.zh: Brady 刚才给了我一个眼色，因为如果你在谈无穷，

cues.en: you can't count infinity,
cues.zh: 你是没法数无穷的，

cues.en: can you? Because it goes on forever.
cues.zh: 对吧？因为它永远延续下去。

cues.en: I think it's a terrible name.
cues.zh: 我觉得这名字糟透了。

cues.en: I prefer to call it listable.
cues.zh: 我更喜欢叫它“可列举的”。

cues.en: Can we list
cues.zh: 我们能列出

cues.en: these numbers? All right, let's do the simple numbers. One,
cues.zh: 这些数字吗？好，先从简单的数字开始。一，

cues.en: two,
cues.zh: 二，

cues.en: three SPEAKER You're not going do all of my jokes. For how long have we got? SPEAKER Ten minutes. SPEAKER All right. Five,
cues.zh: 三 SPEAKER 你不会要把我的笑话全讲完吧。我们还有多长时间？SPEAKER 十分钟。SPEAKER 好。五，

cues.en: six.
cues.zh: 六。

cues.en: So you can list the whole numbers.
cues.zh: 所以你可以把自然数全部列出来。

cues.en: So this is called countable. Listable, I prefer. What about the integers? All the integers. That's all the negative numbers as well. So there's zero. Let's have that. But there's one, and minus one. There's two, and minus two. There's three and minus three. Now,
cues.zh: 这叫做“可数”。我更喜欢叫它“可列举”。那整数呢？所有的整数，也就是把负数也算进来。比如有 0，算上它。还有 1 和 -1，2 和 -2，3 和 -3。那么，

cues.en: that is an infinity as well. And in some sense,
cues.zh: 这也是一种无穷。而且在某种意义上，

cues.en: it's twice as big. Because there seems to be twice as many numbers.
cues.zh: 它好像是两倍大。因为数字的数量看起来翻了一倍。

cues.en: But it is infinity as well. They're both infinity,
cues.zh: 但它也是无穷。它们都是无穷，

cues.en: and they're both the same type of infinity. They both can be listed.
cues.zh: 而且是同一种类型的无穷。它们都可以被列举出来。

cues.en: Perhaps more surprisingly,
cues.zh: 或许更令人惊讶的是，

cues.en: the fractions can be listed as well. But you have to be a bit clever about this. Let's try and list the fractions. I'm going to write out a rectangle.
cues.zh: 分数其实也是可以被列举出来的。不过这得动点脑筋。我们来试着列一下分数。我要写出一个矩形阵列。

cues.en: One divided by one. That's a fraction, that's allowed. Let's have one divided by two,
cues.zh: 1 除以 1。这是个分数，没问题。再来个 1 除以 2，

cues.en: onethree,
cues.zh: 三分之一，

cues.en: onefour,
cues.zh: 四分之一，

cues.en: oneseven.
cues.zh: 七分之一。

cues.en: Okay, that goes on. Let's do the next row and have two at the top. Two over one, two over two, two over three, two over four. Let's do the next one. Three over one,
cues.zh: 好的，就这么排下去。再来下一行，分子用 2。2 除以 1，2 除以 2，2 除以 3，2 除以 4。再来看下一行。3 除以 1，

cues.en: three over two, four over six,
cues.zh: 3 除以 2，4 除以 6，

cues.en: four over seven. Now it goes on, and we can keep going. So here I've made some sort of infinite
cues.zh: 4 除以 7。就这样不断写下去。这样我就排出了某种无限的

cues.en: rectangle array of fractions. Now,
cues.zh: 分数矩形阵列。现在，

cues.en: if I want to make a list like this though,
cues.zh: 但如果我想像刚才那样列成一张表，

cues.en: if
cues.zh: 如果

cues.en: I went row by row,
cues.zh: 我一行一行地数，

cues.en: you're going to have a problem.
cues.zh: 就会遇到问题了。

cues.en: If you go row by row, I'll go this, there's one, onetwo, onethree, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, and I'll keep going forever.
cues.zh: 如果你一行一行来，就会是：1、二分之一、三分之一、四分之一、五分之一、六分之一、七分之一……然后永远也数不完这一行。

cues.en: And I'm never going to reach the second row. I can't list them. Not that way. You can't list them that way. You'll never reach the second row. This is how you list them. Slightly more clever than that.
cues.zh: 我永远也到不了第二行。我没法把它们列出来。不是那样。你没法那样列。你永远到不了第二行。要这样列。比那稍微巧妙一点。

cues.en: You take the diagonal lines.
cues.zh: 你取对角线。

cues.en: Now I can guarantee
cues.zh: 现在我可以保证

cues.en: that every fraction will appear
cues.zh: 每个分数都会出现

cues.en: on one of those diagonal lines. And you list them diagonal by diagonal.
cues.zh: 在其中一条对角线上。你一条对角线一条对角线地列。

cues.en: So that's the first diagonal.
cues.zh: 这是第一条对角线。

cues.en: Then you list the second diagonal. There it is. Then you list the third diagonal. Then you take the fourth diagonal, and the fifth. So eventually, you are going to list every fraction. Every fraction appears on a diagonal, and you're going to list them. Now if you take all the numbers, right? So that's the whole number line. Let's try that. Look. I'm going to draw it. It's a continuous line of numbers. These are all your decimals. You've got zero there in the middle, and you'll get one, and two, and three, but it has a third.
cues.zh: 然后列第二条对角线。就是这样。然后列第三条对角线。接着取第四条、第五条。最终你会把每个分数都列出来。每个分数都出现在某条对角线上，你就把它们列出来。现在如果你取所有数，对吧？这就是整条数轴。我们试试看。看。我来画出来。这是一条连续的数线。这些都是你的小数。中间是零，然后是一、二、三，但它还有三分之一。

cues.en: It will contain pi,
cues.zh: 它会包含 pi，

cues.en: and e, and all the irrational numbers as well.
cues.zh: 还有 e，以及所有无理数。

cues.en: Can you list them? How do you list them? Zero to start with, and then one, but hang on, we've missed a half.
cues.zh: 你能把它们列出来吗？你怎么列？从零开始，然后是一，但等等，我们漏掉了二分之一。

cues.en: So we put in a half. Hang on, we've missed a quarter. We've put in a quarter.
cues.zh: 于是我们加入二分之一。等等，我们漏掉了四分之一。我们加入四分之一。

cues.en: We've missed 0.237.
cues.zh: 我们漏掉了 0.237。

cues.en: So how do you list the real numbers? It turns out you can't.
cues.zh: 那你怎么列出实数？结果是你做不到。

cues.en: And in fact, and rather remarkably,
cues.zh: 而事实上，相当引人注目的是，

cues.en: I can show you that we can't list them, even though we're talking about something so complicated as infinity.
cues.zh: 我可以向你证明我们没法把它们列出来，即使我们谈论的是像无穷这样复杂的东西。

cues.en: Do it, man. We'll need paper. We need an infinite amount of paper here, aren't we? It's
cues.zh: 来吧，伙计。我们需要纸。这里需要无限多的纸，对吧？这是

cues.en: a big topic. Imagine
cues.zh: 个大话题。想象一下

cues.en: we could list all the decimals, right? We can't actually, but pretend we can. What of what would it look like?
cues.zh: 我们可以列出所有小数，对吧？实际上做不到，但假装可以。那会是什么样子？

cues.en: We'll start with all the zero point decimals.
cues.zh: 我们从所有零点几的小数开始。

cues.en: Let's pick some decimals. One, two, one, ....dot.
cues.zh: 选几个小数。一、二、一、……点。

cues.en: Let's pick the next one. Let's say the next one is 221.
cues.zh: 选下一个。假设下一个是221。

cues.en: Next one?
cues.zh: 下一个？

cues.en: And let's take another one here. 00176.
Now I'm going to
cues.zh: 现在我要

cues.en: make a number. This is the number I'm going to make. I'm going to take the diagonals here. I'm going to take this number,
cues.zh: 构造一个数。这就是我要构造的数。我取这里的对角线。取这个数，

cues.en: and this number, and this number, and this and this number.
cues.zh: 还有这个数，这个数，这个和这个数。

cues.en: Okay, and I am going to
cues.zh: 好，然后我要

cues.en: write that down. So what's that number I've made? It's 0 point
cues.zh: 把它写下来。那我构造出的数是什么？是0点

cues.en: Something, something, something.
cues.zh: 某某某。

cues.en: Now, this is my rule.
cues.zh: 现在，这是我的规则。

cues.en: I'm going to make a whole new number from that one. This is the number I'm going to make. If it has a 1,
cues.zh: 我要根据它构造一个全新的数。这就是我要构造的数。如果某位是1，

cues.en: I'm going to change it to a 2.
cues.zh: 我就把它改成2。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 然后

cues.en: if it has a 2,
cues.zh: 如果某位是2，

cues.en: or anything else,
cues.zh: 或其他任何数字，

cues.en: I will change it to a 1.
cues.zh: 我就把它改成1。

cues.en: So let's try that. So I'm going to turn this into
cues.zh: 来试试。我要把这个变成

cues.en: not a point. So if it has a one, I'm going to turn it into a two. If it's anything else, I'm going turn it into a one. So that will be a one. I'm going to change the one here into a two.
cues.zh: 不是点。如果某位是1，就改成2。如果是其他任何数字，就改成1。所以这里会是1。我把这里的1改成2。

cues.en: I'm going change that one into a one. I'm going to change that one into a two. That was my rule. And I make something new.
cues.zh: 我把那个1改成1。我把那个1改成2。这就是我的规则。于是我造出了新东西。

cues.en: That does not appear on the list.
cues.zh: 这不在列表上。

cues.en: That number is completely different from everything else on the list because
cues.zh: 这个数字和列表上的其他数字完全不同，因为

cues.en: it's not the first number because it's different in the first place.
cues.zh: 它不是第一个数字，因为它在第一位就不同。

cues.en: It's not the second number because it's different in the second place.
cues.zh: 它不是第二个数字，因为它在第二位就不同。

cues.en: It's not the third number because it's different in the third place. It's not the fourth number because it's different in the fourth place. It's not the fifth number, because it's different in the fifth place. You've made a number that's not on that list.
cues.zh: 它不是第三个数字，因为它在第三位就不同。它不是第四个数字，因为它在第四位就不同。它不是第五个数字，因为它在第五位就不同。你构造出了一个不在列表上的数字。

cues.en: And so, you can't list all the decimals,
cues.zh: 所以，你无法列出所有小数，

cues.en: in which case it is uncountable.
cues.zh: 因此它是不可数的。

cues.en: It is unlistable.
cues.zh: 它是无法列出的。

cues.en: And that means it's a whole new type of infinity,
cues.zh: 这意味着它是一种全新类型的无穷，

cues.en: a bigger type of infinity. SPEAKER Surely we could, James. Because all we've got to do is keep doing your game, and making them, and adding them to the list. And if we keep doing that, why don't we get there eventually? SPEAKER But you could then create another number that won't be on that list. So the guy who came up with this was a German mathematician called Cantor.
cues.zh: 一种更大的无穷。 演讲者：我们当然可以，James。因为我们只需一直玩你的游戏，不断构造它们，并把它们加到列表上。如果我们一直这样做，为什么最终不能到达呢？ 演讲者：但你随后又可以构造出另一个不在列表上的数字。所以提出这个想法的人是一位德国数学家，叫 Cantor。

cues.en: Cantor lived round about the turn of the twentieth century. He was ridiculed
cues.zh: Cantor 生活在二十世纪之交前后。他因为这个

cues.en: for this. For this idea that there are different types of infinity,
cues.zh: 而遭到嘲笑。因为这个想法——存在不同类型的无穷，

cues.en: he was called a charlatan.
cues.zh: 他被称为骗子。

cues.en: And he was called it was nonsense, it was called.
cues.zh: 它被称为胡说八道，它被称为。

cues.en: And poor old Cantor,
cues.zh: 而可怜的老 Cantor，

cues.en: was treated really badly by his contemporaries.
cues.zh: 受到同时代人极差的对待。

cues.en: And he spent
cues.zh: 他花了很多

cues.en: a lot of his later life
cues.zh: 晚年的时光

cues.en: in and out of mental institutions,
cues.zh: 在精神病院进进出出，

cues.en: where
cues.zh: 最终

cues.en: he died in the end. Near the end of his life, it was recognized. It was true, it was recognized, and he had all the
cues.zh: 在那里去世。在他生命的最后阶段，它得到了承认。它是真的，它得到了承认，他得到了所有

cues.en: recognition that he deserved. SPEAKER And now he's on SPEAKER And now he's on number number foul, the greatest accolade of all. George Cantor.
cues.zh: 他应得的认可。 演讲者：现在他上了 演讲者：现在他上了第四名，最伟大的荣誉。George Cantor。
